gold_assessment.reasoning: Gold states: diarrhea and central abdominal pain for 3 days. Generated CC includes only 3-day history of diarrhea; the abdominal pain component and duration of pain are not captured anywhere as part of the chief complaint.

Watery diarrhea 5–6 times per day, only fluid, no blood, and sensation of incomplete evacuation are not mentioned in any generated HPI or ROS fact. Only increased stool frequency/urgency is present, without these specific characteristics or counts.

Gold describes central abdominal pain present since onset, with no radiation, and characterized as mild-to-moderate tenderness and cramping. Generated HPI-001 notes central crampy pain under the umbilicus and partial relief with bowel movements but does not include the temporal aspect ('since onset'), absence of radiation, or explicit mild-to-moderate tenderness. Key elements are missing, so the gold fact is not fully captured.

Gold specifies that eating and drinking provoke nausea and a feeling of gas. Generated facts mention nausea (HPI-003) but do not link it to eating/drinking or mention the gas sensation, so the full gold content is not captured.

Gold states: some vomiting and now unable to tolerate fluids or solids. Generated HPI-002 documents a single vomiting episode after fruit and no blood, but does not state being currently unable to tolerate fluids/solids or multiple episodes. Thus, key features (ongoing intolerance, multiple vomiting episodes) are missing.

Gold: ate this morning and vomited immediately. Generated HPI-002: vomited once this morning after eating fruit, no blood. The immediate timing after eating is similar but the gold does not mention fruit or absence of blood. Because generation adds specifics not present in gold and omits the 'immediately' emphasis, it is not a direct capture of the gold wording; considered omitted for strict matching.

Gold: patient feels and appears dehydrated. Generated HPI-009 only notes fluid intake may be low, and no generated physical finding describes dehydration. The subjective and objective dehydration are not captured.

Gold: frequency of bowel movements has made the patient unable to go to work. Generated HPI-004: increased stool frequency and urgency preventing work and requiring being near a toilet. This covers the functional impact on work and ties it to stool frequency, matching the gold fact.

Gold: if symptoms do not improve, visit GP surgery. Generated fu-001/plan-004: seek in-person review if no improvement or worsening. This covers the follow-up instruction.
